title: On-prem audit relay: customer-controlled retention, KMS/HSM integration, and VPC-forwarding support
creator: Diego Torres
description:
Goal: Implement a robust, auditable, and customer-configurable forwarding pipeline for audit logs in Private/VPC and on-prem deployments. Provide customers the ability to forward audit events to their own storage endpoints (S3-compatible, on-prem object stores, Kafka, syslog/nginx, or SFTP) with configurable retention policies, envelope encryption using customer-managed KMS or HSM, and strong attestations for integrity.

Background: Private deployments currently capture audit events to the local control plane audit store. Enterprise customers require forwarding into their secure environments or customer-managed storage for retention and compliance. This ticket consolidates the architecture, implementation plan, and rollout for: (1) protocol adapters for forwarding, (2) KMS/HSM integration for envelope encryption, (3) retention and lifecycle controls owned by the customer, and (4) admin RBAC controls to manage forwarding endpoints and keys.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement cross-account IAM roles for public cloud S3 data-plane access (handled separately), nor does it replace system-level security logging for node-level OS events.

Design summary and trade-offs: 
- Forwarding adapters: support S3 (AWS, S3-compatible), HTTPS POST (webhook with mutual TLS), Kafka (plaintext and TLS), syslog (RFC5424), and SFTP. Each adapter will run as a separate connector process inside the customer control plane. Trade-off: supporting many protocols increases maintenance; prioritized order: S3-compatible, HTTPS/mTLS, Kafka, syslog, SFTP.
- Delivery semantics: best-effort at-least-once with deduplication metadata. Reasons: strict once semantics would require distributed transactional support and increase latency. Deduplication window is limited to 24 hours and uses event-id + sequence token.
- Failure modes and backpressure: connectors will expose circuit-breaker status in the Console and use bounded local queues with persistent retry (disk-backed). For severe backpressure, connector changes to 'paused' state with admin notification and optional internal archive (control-plane locked) to avoid data loss.
- Encryption: two-layer model. Data plane encryption in transit (TLS/mTLS) + envelope encryption at rest before sending to customer storage. Provide interfaces for customer-managed KMS (via KMIP/HSM or cloud KMS APIs) and an option to import wrapping keys. For HSM support, connector delegates wrapping key ops to the local HSM via PKCS#11 or KMIP. Trade-off: HSM integration increases ops surface area but is required for FIPS/HITRUST customers.
- Audit schema and versioning: use JSONL records with top-level fields: event_id, timestamp, actor, resource, action, outcome, metadata.version = "auditv2". Provide a schema registry URL in Console and a conversion shim for older auditv1 events.
- RBAC and admin controls: only users in the "audit-admin" role (RBAC v2) may create/modify forwarding endpoints and key bindings. All changes to forwarding configs are themselves written to the audit log with immutable versioning.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Spec & Threat Model (done): design doc and threat model reviewed with SecEng. Link in attachments.
2) Connector framework (week 1-2): implement pluggable connector interface with lifecycle management and queueing layer.
3) S3-compatible adapter + envelope encryption (week 3): support signed PUT multipart, resumable uploads, and server-side-encryption-by-customer (SSE-C) shim.
4) HTTPS webhook w/ mTLS and delivery acknowledgements (week 4).
5) Kafka / syslog adapters (week 5).
6) KMS/HSM integration: support cloud KMS APIs and a KMIP client for on-prem HSMs (week 3-6 parallel).
7) Console + RBAC v2: UI for creating endpoints, key bindings, retention policies, and showing connector health + audit trail (week 4-6).
8) E2E tests, failure-injection, and runbook (week 6-7).
9) Canary rollout to internal staging then opt-in customer pilot (week 8).

Operational considerations and observability: 
- Metrics: per-connector TPS, queue depth, retry rate, last-success, and last-error with reason codes normalized.
- Tracing: propagate Redwood request-id and connector-span IDs, expose in Console with links to logs.
- Alerting: create SLOs for delivery latency and error rate; fire PagerDuty for sustained failure above threshold.
- Data residency: respect deployment region; connectors will not forward outside configured allowed CIDR ranges unless explicitly permitted by the customer config.

Security controls and review notes: 
- Ensure key material never leaves customer-managed HSM unwrapped. When integrating cloud KMS, use envelope keys and never persist plaintext data keys.
- Implement ACLs on connector config objects; every config change emits an immutable audit entry.
- Conduct cryptographic review for KMIP and PKCS#11 interactions.

Rollout and migration plan: 
- Phase 1: internal staging rollout, validate adapters against mock S3 and KMIP HSM emulator.
- Phase 2: invited customer pilot with strict monitoring and manual fallback.
- Phase 3: GA for Dedicated and Private customers with opt-in migration scripts and runbook.

Open questions: 
- Should we provide an auto-expiry purge job for customer-controlled retention or leave retention enforcement to customer storage? (Prefer hybrid: policy-enforcement field that can be either "enforce" or "advisory" to support customers who cannot permit us deleting objects.)
- What guarantees do SOC/Legal require around provenance headers? (Need input from Security & Compliance)
- Decision on deduplication window length (default 24h proposed).

Success criteria: 
- Pilot customers successfully receive audit events to their storage with envelope encryption and can validate integrity.
- Connector metrics are visible in Console and alerts exist for delivery regressions.
- Security review signed off and runbook validated by SRE.

Delivery artifacts: design doc, threat model, runbook, API schema, connector SDK, PRs.
